clue.text: Christian name of poet such as George

definitions.meaning: a boy's given name, as in the writer ... Read or the novelist H. G. Wells
George ... was the seventeenth-century English metaphysical poet of The Temple

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a common forename and the surname of the devotional poet George, so one word fits both readings.

clue.text: Emma's man' in Elsinore

parts.note: Emma Hamilton's lover was Admiral Nelson, whose first name is shared by Hamlet's loyal friend at the Danish castle of Elsinore

explanation.surface: A woman's partner turns up at the Danish castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Emma Hamilton's lover was Lord Nelson, first name Horatio; Hamlet, set in Elsinore, has his friend of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename links Nelson, Emma Hamilton's lover, and Hamlet's faithful friend at the Danish court.

clue.text: Charles II's favourite place in England

definitions.meaning: the rakish John Wilmot, Earl of ..., was a favourite courtier of Charles II

explanation.definitionFit: Charles II's favoured courtier was the Earl of that title, named after the Kent cathedral city.

clue.text: Facilitated 'rest with key

parts.note: ease means rest and leisure, as in at ease
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone made things simpler by resting with a key in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces; keys in crosswords are often musical, A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease a task is to make it easier, smoothing its way.

clue.text: Having full complement of hands, unlike Captain Hook.

definitions.text: Having full complement of hands, unlike Captain Hook.

parts.words: Having full complement of hands, unlike Captain Hook.
parts.note: Captain Hook in Peter Pan lost a hand to the crocodile, so has only one; the phrase also means aggressive and ready to fight

explanation.surface: A ship has its full crew, unlike Peter Pan's pirate captain's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' suggests sailors on Hook's ship, but means the body parts: Hook has only one. The answer also means vigorous or pugnacious.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally having both fists, and figuratively tough and vigorous, as a brawler is.

clue.text: Special day to organise bash, with bat

indicators.note: to organise something is to put it into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone plans a party, armed with a bat, for a day of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to organise' rearranges BASH and BAT together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly holy day of rest in Jewish and Christian tradition is a special day.

clue.text: Take turn to sort letters

definitions.meaning: to relieve someone at a task, taking a stint
to put letters in their correct order to form a word

explanation.definitionFit: To relieve another worker for a period is one sense, and naming a word's letters in order is the other.

clue.text: Like the Camptown nag having taken a short cut

definitions.meaning: the song Camptown Races has the line about betting on the bob-tail nag
with a tail that has been docked or cut short

explanation.definitionFit: The horse in Stephen Foster's song had a docked tail, and an animal so cut short is described this way.

clue.text: A look of being indifferent

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A glance shows someone to be uninterested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' links; the pieces run A, LO, OF in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distant and detached, keeping apart from others, seems indifferent.

clue.text: Dogged policeman gets the title right

parts.note: a handle is slang for a title or name, as in a handle to one's name

explanation.surface: A persistent officer is finally awarded the proper rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' reads as tenacious, but means accompanied by a dog: a police dog's minder. 'gets' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer working with a dog is its trainer and controller.

clue.text: Dances 'with a girl's best friend

definitions.meaning: to rock is to dance to rock and roll, so dances means moves to that beat
the song says diamonds are a girl's best friend

explanation.surface: A dancer moves with her most treasured companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock as a verb is a dance step, and in slang diamonds are rocks, the jewels the song praises.

clue.text: Gone with. the Wind — novel originally found excessive

parts.note: something gone or finished is over
to blow is to move as the wind does, a gust

indicators.note: originally means at its beginning, so the first letter of novel is taken

explanation.surface: A famous novel turns out, on reflection, to be too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title Gone with the Wind splits apart: 'Gone' and 'Wind' are pieces, with 'with the' linking; 'originally' takes the first letter of 'novel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overblown style is inflated or overdone, exaggerated well past what is needed.

clue.text: Circulatory system forcing one to walk to work

definitions.text: Circulatory system forcing one to walk to work

parts.words: Circulatory system forcing one to walk to work
parts.note: reads like a commuting scheme or the blood's circuit, but describes a belt going round and round that makes you walk on the spot, or a daily grind

explanation.surface: A plan for getting about obliges a commuter to go to the office on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulatory' suggests blood, but it means going round in a loop; 'walk to work' is both literal and the drudgery of a daily routine.
explanation.definitionFit: The looping belt or wheel walked on to drive machinery, or figuratively a tedious routine of work.

clue.text: Deplorable and not quite legal

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so one letter is lost from the synonym of legal

parts.note: legal means permitted by law, lawful

explanation.surface: Some conduct is shameful and only just within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the L from the start of the synonym for 'legal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful or very bad is deplorable.

clue.text: Dismissed, soldiers about turn -in target area

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

indicators.note: an about turn is a military about-face, so the soldiers' letters are read the other way

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops are sent off parade and wheel round towards the range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about turn' turns RE round to ER. The definition describes the outermost ring of an archery or shooting target, the one furthest from the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target the outermost scoring ring is so named, and a shot landing there is in that area.

clue.text: Beak who could have uncovered -plot against Caesar?.

definitions.text: Beak who could have uncovered -plot against Caesar?

parts.words: Beak who could have uncovered -plot against Caesar?
parts.note: beak is slang for nose; a Roman who could nose out the conspiracy of Brutus would be a sniffer from Rome

explanation.surface: A magistrate might have exposed the conspiracy to murder Julius Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which the surface suggests, and also for a nose; a curved, aquiline nose bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent nose with a high bridge is so called, and a Roman nosing out the plot would be one too.

clue.text: It fixes the margins on which a writer operates

definitions.text: It fixes the margins on which a writer operates

parts.words: It fixes the margins on which a writer operates
parts.note: sounds like a publisher's editor or financier setting profit margins for an author, but describes the typewriter key that sets column stops

explanation.surface: Someone or something settles the terms under which an author works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'margins' suggests profit and 'writer' an author; the writer is a typewriter and the margins are page edges, set by its tab key.
explanation.definitionFit: A device on a typewriter that sets stops for columns and indents, the tab key mechanism.

clue.text: Bravo! Complain about the food

parts.note: bully is an old exclamation of approval, as in bully for you
to beef about something is to grumble about it

explanation.surface: Someone cheers, then moans about the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Corned beef in tins, the army's staple ration, is known in Britain by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned corned beef, especially as a soldier's ration, is the food meant.

clue.text: Serious actor, skilled at reading — parts

indicators.note: parts as a verb means splits up, so the letters of at reading are separated and regrouped

explanation.surface: A grave actor is an expert at reading roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like stage roles but signals breaking up AT READING; 'skilled' belongs to the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who specialises in roles in serious plays of downfall and death is a tragic player.

clue.text: Like a spot of snooker -pink is on for a start?.

definitions.text: Like a spot of snooker -pink is on for a start?

parts.words: Like a spot of snooker -pink is on for a start?
parts.note: at the start of a snooker frame the reds are racked in a triangle with the pink ball on its spot just at the apex

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a quick game of snooker, aiming at the pink to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the fifteen reds start racked in a triangle, the pink on its spot at the apex; the shape is that of an Egyptian tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like the Egyptian tombs, triangular in profile, as the racked reds are.

clue.text: Chap who throws a pot

definitions.meaning: the player who throws the ball in baseball
a jug or large vessel for pouring

explanation.definitionFit: A baseball bowler and a jug for liquids share the name.

clue.text: Play the medic to a master

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A doctor stages a show for a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece written for the stage, as is any work of theatre.

clue.text: Article on Alighieri — take it slowly

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: Someone advises a reader of an essay on the Italian poet to go at a gentle pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces; the definition is a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term marks a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Athenian victim once of ingratitude — it shows

indicators.note: it shows means the answer is on display within the words victim once

explanation.surface: A citizen of Athens who was once the victim of ingratitude reveals it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it shows' points to letters on view in 'victim once'. Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is the nobleman ruined by ungrateful friends, so 'of ingratitude' colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of Shakespeare's Timon of Athens was a citizen of that Greek city.

clue.text: Looked unhappy with bike

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means sulked or brooded

explanation.definitionFit: To have sulked is the verb, and a light motorised cycle is the noun.

clue.text: The date of a twenties style musical

definitions.meaning: the person you are dating, your partner on a date
Sandy Wilson's 1953 show pastiching 1920s musical comedy

explanation.definitionFit: A girl's date is her young man, and Sandy Wilson's pastiche of a 1920s show bears the same title.

clue.text: Not knowing the happiness of Gray

definitions.text: Not knowing the happiness of Gray

parts.words: Not knowing the happiness of Gray
parts.note: Thomas Gray's ode ends where ignorance is this, so not knowing is called happiness

explanation.surface: Someone is unaware of how happy a man named Gray is.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College ends: where ignorance is ..., 'tis folly to be wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's line equates ignorance with perfect happiness, joy that comes of not knowing.

clue.text: Field-work about a Biblical place

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Dan was a city in northern Israel, as in from Dan to Beersheba

explanation.surface: A dig in the field turns up something about a site in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field-work' suggests a dig, but means a military fortification in the field, a V-shaped rampart.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortification with two walls meeting in a salient angle was built as a field defence.

clue.text: The pony is jogging to induce relaxation

indicators.note: jogging shakes something about, so the letters of the pony is are jostled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pony trotting along lulls its rider into calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' jostles the nine letters of THE PONY IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone into a trance is to bring about a deep, relaxed sleep-like state.

clue.text: Condescend to call a European

indicators.note: call here means say the word out, so the sound of the European is what counts

parts.note: a Dane, a native of Denmark, is a European

explanation.surface: Someone stoops so low as to telephone a person from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' signals saying DANE out loud; 'to' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to lower oneself to do something thought beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: Compensation for a tiring repeat

definitions.meaning: compensation means amends or reparation for a wrong
read as attiring again: to dress once more

explanation.surface: Damages are paid for an exhausting rerun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tiring' is to be read as 'attiring', clothing; doing that again is re-dressing. 'for' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation for a wrong is its remedy, and putting clothes on again is a second clothing.

clue.text: Pay for betrothed to incorporate name

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so N goes inside the word for betrothed

parts.note: a man who is betrothed is engaged, a fiance

explanation.surface: An engaged man pays up, taking on a new surname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to incorporate' places N inside FIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fund something is to provide the money for it.
